questions.question: What does dialogue state tracking maintain across turns?
options: A free-text history only
A slot-value dictionary representing the user's current goal, updated after every turn
An embedding of the conversation — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail
A POS-tagged transcript
questions.explanation: DST keeps a structured slot-value map that the backend can act on.

questions.question: What does Joint Goal Accuracy (JGA) measure?
options: Fraction of turns where every slot is exactly correct (all-or-nothing)
Average slot accuracy, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases
Latency per turn
Cosine similarity
questions.explanation: JGA is the strict per-turn match across all slots; per-slot accuracy is more lenient.

questions.question: Why does regenerating the whole state from history each turn handle user corrections naturally?
options: It uses fewer tokens, because one plausible output is sufficient production evidence, before defining the measurement, acceptance threshold, or rollback path
It runs on GPU
It avoids embeddings
Reading the full history lets the model re-derive the final state including 'actually...' corrections without explicit rollback logic
questions.explanation: Full-history regeneration absorbs corrections by recomputing the final state from the entire conversation.

questions.question: Which 2026 pattern gives a guaranteed-valid slot dict in 5 lines of code?
options: Hand-written regex, before defining the measurement, acceptance threshold, or rollback path
BM25 retrieval
LLM + Instructor + Pydantic schema with constrained or validated output
TF-IDF classifier
questions.explanation: Pydantic schema + Instructor validates the LLM's state output against the slot ontology automatically.

questions.question: Why version your DST schema?
options: Adding new slots post-hoc invalidates older training data and breaks longitudinal evaluation
Required by JSON
Reduce token count — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases
Speed gains
questions.explanation: Unversioned schema changes silently break training data alignment and eval comparability.

questions.question: Why must DST for compliance-sensitive domains include a rule-based check alongside LLM extraction?
options: Rules avoid embeddings, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases, because one plausible output is sufficient production evidence
LLM-only DST can mis-extract destructive parameters (amount, account, date); a rules layer enforces deterministic constraints
LLMs are slower
Rules are multilingual
questions.explanation: Compliance domains require deterministic enforcement; rules catch slot errors that LLMs introduce.
